legalNotice.title: Legal notice
legalNotice.intro: Who publishes Moi Président, what the game is and is not, and what it does with your data.

paragraphs.text: Moi Président is a humorous and parodic work of fiction, loosely inspired by political news. The opponents, the parties, the events, the dialogues and the slogans are the publisher's creations; the names of the opponents and the parties are deliberately twisted. The game reports no real fact, statement or position of any existing person, and expresses no opinion of the publisher on a person, a party or a vote.

The game gives no voting instruction. It is not affiliated with any governmental organisation, political party or activist association. It has no link with any candidate, movement, media outlet or polling institute, and is neither endorsed nor funded by any of them.

paragraphs.lead: A simplified model, with its own biases.
paragraphs.text: The game reduces political life to nine families, five axes and a few categories of voters. The opponents' positions are estimates by the game's team. The effects of actions, events and measures are game rules, not forecasts: they reflect design choices that others would have made differently. The game is not a source of electoral information: do not base a vote on its figures.

The game's press review sometimes covers tragedies: disasters, riots, violence, attacks. They are rare and all fictional, inspired by real debates without their names or places: no victim is named or described, no image is shown, and nothing rewards taking advantage of them.

The scores, rankings, "polls", trends and results shown in the game come from a simulation. It starts from real polls (see "Notice of the simulation") and transforms them in every game: its figures measure nobody's opinion and predict neither the voting intentions nor the result of the real election. French law no. 77-808 of 19 July 1977 treats a vote simulation made from polls as a poll{filed, select, yes {: its notice can be consulted at the Commission des sondages} other {}}.

paragraphs.lead: The die, the mark of the game's figures.
paragraphs.text: The icon of a die, a square with dots, goes with the data, figures and values the game simulates, even without the word "fictional": they must not be taken for reality.
Screenshots of the game must not be presented as real polls or real results.

notice.title: Notice of the simulation

paragraphs.text: In the campaign's game space, the app provides fictional data: any figure that cites no source is a game figure, and it is fictional.

Simulation made by Matthieu Compérat (Cosmic Studio), on his own account, from 23 polls of first-round voting intentions for the 2027 presidential election, carried out by Ifop, Elabe, Harris Interactive, Cluster17, YouGov, OpinionWay and Odoxa, and published in September and October 2026. The game transforms them in every game: its figures are fictional.
Every poll has margins of error. The margins shown in the game are a game rule.

notice.filed: Anyone can consult the notice of this simulation at the Commission des sondages.
notice.frozen: Data frozen in version {version} of the game.

paragraphs.text: The starting voting intentions come from polls published in September and October 2026, then the simulation transforms them. They are not updated during the game and may have changed a lot since. For up-to-date figures, see the notices published by the Commission des sondages: each one names the institute that carried out the poll.

meta.description: Moi Président sends no personal data to the publisher: what the game stores on your device, its permissions, the campaign kit and your recourse.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what the game Moi Président does with your personal data.

data.title: What Moi Président does with your data

paragraphs.text: No personal data about you is sent to the publisher: the game has no account, no advertising and no audience measurement. Your candidate name, your photo, your slogan, your poster, your party, your campaign and your preferences (language, theme) are stored only on your device.

Camera: only to take the photo of your poster, when you ask. You can refuse this access or withdraw it in your device's settings. To choose a photo, the game opens your device's picker: it receives the photo you choose only, with no access to your other photos.
If you share your poster, the file goes to the app you choose in your device's share menu; the publisher receives no copy.
You delete your poster in the app; uninstalling the app erases all the data.

The kit is optional. The game only connects for it: once, at the start of your first new campaign, to offer it to you; when you open its page, download it or update it; and, once the kit is installed, at most once a week when the game opens, to find out whether a new edition exists. Its files come from GitHub, which then receives the IP address of your device, like any server. The game sends no account, no identifier and no cookie.
If a future feature were to transmit data, this policy would be updated before it goes live, and you would be informed.

support@gocosmic.dev. You can refer a matter to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC, Switzerland), or to the data protection authority of your country of residence (in France, the CNIL).

kitLicences.title: Moi Président campaign kit: licences
kitLicences.intro:
Publisher: Matthieu Compérat, trading as Cosmic Studio
The kit repository (github.com/Mitchnsun/kit-de-campagne) and its Releases carry the two parts of the kit and the prompts of its illustrations, under different terms. The manifest of each edition (manifest.json) repeats the credits and the licence of each part; for an edition, its manifest prevails.

sections.title: 1. Briefing data (part "briefings")
body: Each figure keeps the licence of its source. The file of each indicator names the producer, the publication, the licence and the date of each source.

items: Most French public sources (Insee, ministries, IGN for the ADMIN EXPRESS COG CARTO map) are under the Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab). Any reuse mentions the source and the date of its last update.

Eurostat data may be reused, commercially too, provided the source is acknowledged ("Source: Eurostat") and any changes are indicated. Data that Eurostat attributes to another source may not be reused commercially. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice

UNHCR datasets (Refugee Data Finder) are under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), with UNHCR's terms of use for datasets: any reuse credits "UNHCR Refugee Population Statistics Database", indicates any changes and links to these terms; it does not suggest that UNHCR takes part in, supports or endorses the game, and uses neither its name nor its emblem as a mark. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ https://www.unhcr.org/what-we-do/reports-and-publications/data-and-statistics/terms-use-datasets
Figures from other producers (CITEPA, polling institutes…) are quoted with their source; no file from these producers is redistributed.

body: The selection, the layout and the "Good to know" notes written by the publisher are released under the Open Licence 2.0: https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/open-licence.pdf
Requested attribution, in addition to the source of each figure: "Moi Président, campaign kit, <month> <year> edition".
The data are dated extracts, provided with no warranty of accuracy or of being up to date. Their producers neither prepared nor endorsed this kit.

sections.title: 2. Illustrations (part "illustrations")
body: The illustrations are AI-generated; the manifest of each edition names the tool used. This part also covers the images of the illustrations/ folder. They are published to be shown in the game Moi Président. The kit repository (github.com/Mitchnsun/kit-de-campagne) grants no licence to reuse them.
The scenes and characters are fictional. Any resemblance to a real person is unintended.

sections.title: 3. Prompts (folder prompts/)
body: The texts of the prompts/ folder, the prompt template and the generation sheets of the images, are written by the publisher and released under the Open Licence 2.0: https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/open-licence.pdf
